label: Given the definition, surveying why non-checkers defer yields three irreducible grounds: legal constitution with sanction, voluntary adoption, or survival under contest

defeaters.description: The trichotomy is neither clearly exhaustive nor clearly distinct. Deference grounded in demonstrated track record or expertise (a pilot, a surgeon, a weather service) settles questions for non-checkers without legal office, without the deferrer having "chosen" in any meaningful sense, and without the claim ever having been openly contested by the deferrer's peers; deference grounded in tradition or charisma is another candidate. And the categories blend: legal offices exist because a political community chose to constitute them, and science operates through offices (journals, funders, degree-granting institutions) whose holders are sanctionable. If the categories overlap or omit cases, "each fails alone and the other two repair it" loses its clean structure.

label: Repeated capture of single-locus regulators, reversed only by exit or external challenge, shows office alone is capturable and names its repair
Guild and diaspora trust stayed in-group until legal recourse and shared dispute forums let it reach strangers
Fake or costless challengers hollow out open challenge; identity/accountability and independent dissent venues restore it

If the three sources are exhaustive and each one's solo failure is repaired by the other two, and working cross-border regimes already exhibit this pattern without coercion, the best explanation of durable stranger-trust is the three combined, not a fourth office

defeaters.description: The cross-border regimes cited as working without a global authority (standards bodies, PKI root programs, arbitration) actually free-ride on background coercive states: arbitration awards are worthless without national courts that enforce them, browser root programs rest on a handful of firms subject to antitrust and consumer-protection law, and standards bodies are backed by procurement mandates. So the examples may show that cross-border trust needs coercive offices doing the heavy lifting underneath, which is closer to the view the thesis rejects. Moreover, the pairwise repairs may fail jointly: a single well-resourced actor can capture offices, dominate the relevant communities, and flood challenge venues at once, and a shared information infrastructure can collapse all three together.

label: Since the combined sources suffice and authority as defined works by being believed rather than by compelling, global stranger-trust needs the three working across borders, with influence but no coercive power

defeaters.description: The step from "the three sources suffice" to "no new global authority is needed, only influence without compulsion" assumes the global trust problem is a problem of belief. Many of the hardest cross-border problems (pandemic reporting, emissions accounting, financial contagion) are problems of compliance and free-riding: parties may fully believe the authoritative word and still defect because defection pays. If so, an arrangement that can only be believed addresses a different question than the one that motivates calls for a global authority, and the conclusion does not follow from the premises even if they are true.
